urls.title: Audio Blackbox: Past Recorder for Android
urls.description: Audio Blackbox is an open-source retroactive audio recorder for Android: an audio dashcam that keeps the last minutes of sound in RAM, so you can save the riff, quote or instructions you just heard. Audio stays in RAM until you tap Save or start Live, and your recordings never leave your phone.

jsonLd.alternateName: Audio Blackbox: Past Recorder for Android
jsonLd.description: Audio Blackbox is an open-source Android app that continuously keeps the last minutes of sound in RAM and writes them to local storage when you explicitly tap Save or start Live. The buffer starts at 5 minutes, in 5-minute steps, up to the app's safe memory limit for the selected quality. There is no product-imposed duration cap; Settings shows the current limit.

featureList: Just played a riff worth keeping, or said an idea out loud? Tap Save and Audio Blackbox writes the buffered audio since your last save (the whole buffer the first time) to a local file. Live saves the buffered audio from before the tap and continues in a single file: .aac (ADTS) with AAC (default), playable while recording, or .ogg with Opus, which you must wait until recording ends to play. Live recording time is limited to 2 hours on the free plan, then the file is saved automatically. The file can exceed 2 hours because it includes the buffered past. A one-time Pro unlock removes the live time limit. Save audio format is free, with no Pro unlock required: AAC (default) saves .m4a files with Save, or choose Opus (.ogg) for both Save and Live. AAC (.m4a): wider compatibility. Opus (.ogg): smaller voice files. Some players and messaging apps may not open them. With AAC selected: Live stays AAC (.aac), playable while recording. Wait until recording ends to play Opus audio. If the app closes unexpectedly, saved audio may be recoverable, but the ending may be lost and some players may not open the file. On reopening after an unexpected close, Opus audio already written is recovered; the incomplete final Ogg page is discarded, so the ending may be lost. Opus may be unavailable on some devices; the option is disabled with the reason shown.

The app itself sends no audio or usage analytics. Google Play Billing (Play services) communicates with Google to process the optional purchase and check entitlement; its library also sends its own usage and error diagnostics. No ads, account or cloud audio storage.
Zero disk I/O and zero IPC allocations on the audio capture thread. Guaranteed single-writer synchronization eliminates dropouts and GC pauses.

When another foreground app takes the microphone, Android silences our stream rather than failing it. The service detects that directly and pauses, then resumes the moment the mic is free. The gap is preserved as true silence, so exported timestamps never drift.
Foreground service with active notification and guided manufacturer battery-optimization bypass keeps recording uninterrupted even with the screen off.
Listen, seek, delete, and share your saved .m4a / .aac (AAC) or .ogg (Opus) recordings through the Android share sheet. A home-screen widget starts or stops recording with one tap.

mainEntity.name: Is there an Android app that records the last 5 minutes of audio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The buffer starts at 5 minutes, in 5-minute steps, up to the app's safe memory limit for the selected quality. There is no product-imposed duration cap; Settings shows the current limit.

mainEntity.name: How can I save audio from before I pressed record?

acceptedAnswer.text: A normal recorder cannot do this, because it only starts capturing when you press record. With Audio Blackbox, you turn on continuous recording once and it keeps the most recent minutes in a rolling RAM buffer, replacing the oldest audio with the newest. When something worth keeping just happened, tap Save to write those minutes to a file. Audio is written to storage when you tap Save or start Live.

mainEntity.name: What is a retroactive or always-on buffer recorder?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a recorder that keeps capturing into a fixed-size memory buffer, so you can save what was already said instead of only what comes after you press record. Live saves the buffered audio from before the tap and continues in a single file: .aac (ADTS) with AAC (default), playable while recording, or .ogg with Opus, which you must wait until recording ends to play. Live recording time is limited to 2 hours on the free plan, then the file is saved automatically. The file can exceed 2 hours because it includes the buffered past. A one-time Pro unlock removes the live time limit.

mainEntity.name: How long is the audio buffer, and how much RAM does it use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The buffer starts at 5 minutes, in 5-minute steps, up to the app's safe memory limit for the selected quality. There is no product-imposed duration cap; Settings shows the current limit. At the default Voice preset (16,000 Hz mono) each minute takes about 1.8 MB of RAM, so 30 minutes is about 55 MB. Balanced (32,000 Hz mono) uses twice that per minute and High fidelity (44,100 Hz stereo) about 5.5 times, so the same phone holds a shorter buffer at higher quality. The calculator in the Memory Architecture section of this page shows the RAM for any window and preset.

mainEntity.name: Does Audio Blackbox upload anything, or does it need an internet connection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recording and saving work offline. The app itself sends no audio or usage analytics. Google Play Billing (Play services) communicates with Google to process the optional purchase and check entitlement; its library also sends its own usage and error diagnostics. No ads, account or cloud audio storage.

mainEntity.name: Does it keep recording when the screen is off?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Audio Blackbox runs as a foreground service with a persistent notification, and it includes a guided flow to bypass manufacturer battery optimization, so capture continues uninterrupted with the screen locked.

mainEntity.name: Does an always-on recorder drain the battery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Audio Blackbox was measured on a Samsung Galaxy S25 recording continuously at the Voice preset: with the screen off it used about 1.0% to 1.5% of the battery per hour and under 1% CPU, with no disk writes while buffering. Other phones and settings will give different numbers.

mainEntity.name: Is there an audio dashcam app for Android?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Unlike a hidden recorder, it always shows a notification while it is recording. Recording other people may require their consent, so check your local laws.

mainEntity.name: Can I recover a quote or a lecture explanation I forgot to record?

acceptedAnswer.text: If Audio Blackbox was running, yes. Tap Save and the buffered minutes (at least 5, up to the app's safe memory limit for the selected quality) are written to an .m4a (AAC) or .ogg (Opus) file, even though you never pressed record. Journalists can use it as a backup to their main recorder, and students can keep an explanation they just missed in classes where recording is allowed.

mainEntity.name: Can Audio Blackbox help me remember spoken instructions?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can work as a memory aid. If you just heard directions, instructions or details and lost track of them, save the last minutes and replay them in the built-in player. This can help anyone who often loses track of spoken information, for example people with ADHD. Audio Blackbox is not a medical device.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to record with Audio Blackbox?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on where you are. Use Audio Blackbox for your own conversations and ideas.
